Civil Miscellaneous Petition filed under Section 115 o  condone the delay of 4065 days in filing the appeal  A.S.SR.No.1791 of 2023

Civil Miscellaneous Appeal filed under Section 54 of L  Acquisition Act, 1894 to enhance the compensation amount awarded in https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  Page 1/4  A.
 
 C.M  LAOP.61/2007 dated 18.08.2011 on the file of II Additional Sub Judg S.Thamizharasi vs The Special Thasildhar on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174052200/
1  Villupuram.
 For Appellant/Petitioner : Mr.S.Nararajan  ORDER (The order of the Court was made by Mrs.J.Nisha Banu,J.)
The Civil Miscellaneous Petition petition has been filed to condone the delay of 4065 days in filing the Appeal.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner/appellant.

3. The above appeal has been filed against the award dated 18.08.2011 passed in LAOP.No.61 of 2007 on the file of II Additional Subordinate Court, Villupuram, in and by which, the trial Court had enhanced the market value of the acquired land to Rs.20.10p. per sq.feet x 1/9th share of 2.72.82 hectares and that the appellant/claimant is entitled for interest 9% for the enhanced market value for 1 year from the date of award and thereafter, 15% per annum till realization as contemplated u/s.
28 of the Act.

In addition to that, the appellant/claimant is entitled to 30% solatium on enhanced market value and entitled to claim interest at the rate of 9% till the date of deposit on the amount of solatium (30% of enhanced market value) awarded.

Already the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis &
respondent paid Rs.4,55,732/- and after deducting the same, the balance was directed to be paid to the claimant within a period of three months.
4. The award was passed on 18.08.2011.
The Appellant had slept over the matter for more than twelve years and now has filed the present appeal for enhancement of compensation.
5. The delay is enormous and we are also not satisfied with the reasons stated in the affidavit for condoning the delay in filing the appeal.
Therefore, we are not inclined to condone the delay and even on merits, we are not inclined to entertain the appeal.
Hence, the condone delay petition stands dismissed.
Consequently, the Appeal Suit is rejected at the SR stage itself and the connected civil miscellaneous petition is closed.
No costs.
(J.N.B,J.)
